h: Violent psychosis, nystagmus, drooling after drug use: substance?
p: PCP causes agitation, violence, vertical or horizontal nystagmus, analgesia and hypertension; treat with benzodiazepines.

h: First-line antihypertensive in a Black patient?
p: Current hypertension guidelines recommend thiazides or calcium channel blockers first in Black patients; ACE inhibitors are less effective and carry higher angioedema risk.

h: Adolescent athlete with back pain worse on extension, hamstring tightness: diagnosis?
p: Pars interarticularis defect (spondylolysis) allows vertebral slippage (L5 on S1) in gymnasts and weightlifters; 'Scottie dog' collar on oblique film.

h: Chronic insomnia with poor sleep habits: first step?
p: Behavioral measures (consistent schedule, avoiding caffeine, screens and clock-watching) are first line before hypnotics; modafinil treats hypersomnia.

x: keyed regimen (fluoroquinolone) conflicts with current stewardship guidance

h: Anaphylaxis during transfusion in IgA deficiency: how to prevent?
p: IgA-deficient patients have anti-IgA antibodies; use washed cells or blood from IgA-deficient donors. Recurrent sinopulmonary infections are the clue.

h: Acute cluster headache (unilateral tearing, Horner): first-line treatment?
p: Cluster headache: abort with oxygen or sumatriptan; verapamil is first-line prophylaxis. Avoid triggers like alcohol.

h: Painful penile ulcer with ragged edges, negative VDRL: diagnosis?
p: Haemophilus ducreyi causes painful ulcers with tender suppurative inguinal nodes; syphilitic chancres are painless and indurated.

h: Positional pleuritic chest pain relieved by sitting up in advanced CKD: cause?
p: Uremia causes fibrinous pericarditis with friction rub, which improves with dialysis.

a: Meniscal tear or other intra-articular knee disease
p: Baker cyst is synovial fluid dissecting into the gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa; common with meniscal tears, osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
Postmenopausal bleeding needs exclusion of endometrial cancer by office biopsy or transvaginal ultrasound; risks include obesity, unopposed estrogen and PCOS history.

h: Circumferential full-thickness burn with absent distal pulses: next step?
p: Circumferential eschar acts as a tourniquet, compromising perfusion and ventilation (chest); escharotomy releases it, fasciotomy is for compartment syndrome.

x: keyed treatment disputed (habit reversal therapy first-line)

h: Sexually active 17-year-old girl: recommended screening test?
p: Screen sexually active women under 25 yearly with NAAT; cervical cancer screening starts at age 21.

h: Adolescent ovarian mass with elevated beta-hCG and AFP: tumor type?
p: Embryonal carcinoma secretes both hCG and AFP; yolk sac tumors secrete AFP (Schiller-Duval bodies); dysgerminoma has LDH.

x: keyed intervention disputable (oxygen vs smoking cessation)

h: Major depressive episode: first-line drug class?
p: SSRIs are first-line because of safety and tolerability; benzodiazepines do not treat depression and TCAs are dangerous in overdose.

h: Opening snap with low-pitched diastolic rumble and atrial fibrillation: valve lesion?
p: Rheumatic mitral stenosis raises left atrial pressure, causing left atrial enlargement, atrial fibrillation, dyspnea and pulmonary hypertension.
Hyperplasia without atypia usually regresses with progestin therapy; atypical hyperplasia needs hysterectomy because of cancer risk.

h: Single hot nodule with suppressed remaining thyroid: diagnosis?
p: A toxic adenoma autonomously makes thyroid hormone, suppressing TSH and normal tissue (patchy uptake in Graves is diffuse).
